description: Let us create a new paradigm
summary:
TerraIntelligence is a platform that, in its most abstract form, optimizes the cost of doing simulations and future planning for the mission and the time to achieve the mission. It understands your mission (on Mars and the Moon only) and suggests analog Earth sites to do the mission. The analog Earth sites are recommended not only on scientific closeness, but also based on 32 vectors, considering factors such as logistics, cost, etc., making it an ideal decision tool and relevant for the new startup agencies and cost-aware organizations like ISRO. However, the scientific validity is not compromised for cost. It has three more features-

Optimizer that optimizes the similarity gap percentage, that is, suggests ways that, while optimizing the cost, it suggests ways that can reduce the similarity gap percentage, making our observations more relevant for the analogue sites.

Predictor that predicts what risks or failure spots could come into the actual mission due to the similarity gap percentage.

Suggestor that suggests, given your location, your constraints, and your resources, what extra missions you could do to achieve your main mission(the abstracted form of the mission) so that resources and time are not wasted.
details:
Our project, as we intend, is an Earth sites analog finder relevant to the mission and a decision support system for mission planners simulating the mission. Currently, the analogue finders depend on accurate scientific matching; however, this creates a blind spot when many parameters involved in the mission simulation are ignored, leading to an ill mission simulation. We have solved this problem with 32 parameters decision sustained these parameters are primarily divided into 5 categories: terrain, geology, operations, climate, and resources, which eases the mission planner's load of considering the factors involved
We have introduced an adjustability bar which the user can use to customise the weights for the different parameters, thus solving the problem of customisability, as different space agencies have different requirements and constraints.

The platform also compares different sites and what benefit each offers but ultimately gives the final best analogue file based on the factors mentioned above

Regarding the similarity percentage gap many problems occur when the findings on the analogue sites do not match the space missions, leading to mission failure and low trust on conducting experiments on these analogue sites and thus building multibillion dollars lab artificially which makes young startups cost-hungry and thus lead high failure rate thus our application is relevant to the space startups cost aware space agencies and space agencies of emerging economies.
We solve this problem in two ways: first, by giving suggestions through which we can cost-effectively increase similarity percentage, and it also predicts what problem may emerge during the actual mission due to the similarity percentage gap

Another problem that occurs is when a team has reached an analogue Earth site and is left with certain resources, but it cannot figure out what to do next to achieve the mission; thus, the platform at last finds opportunities given your mission, your resources left, and your location to help in the proper utilisation of the resources and decrease the cost

Thus, the benefits of this project in its most abstracted form are to reduce simulation costs and reduce the time to achieve the mission. It also includes ease in decision-making for mission planning.
The platform runs on the following workflow:
1. It first identifies an analogue Earth site based on your mission, then it predicts the risk that emerges due to the similarity gap, then it suggests ways through which we can increase the similarity cost-effectively, and then it identifies the opportunities given your remaining resources, left constraints, location, and mission

It also has a team workspace on which teams can collaborate. At last, the full mission report is generated on a separate tab.

Our vision is to create more comprehensive decisions for this platform and pioneer the analogue Earth sites for different missions and thus, ultimately act as a meta platform with the help of which other companies and missions could be built efficiently,

The tech stack we have used for the framework is Next.js and React; for styling and UI: Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui; for icons and motion: Lucide icons and Framer Motion; for deployment: Google AI Studio; for API and logic: Python and FastAPI; for AI and LLMs: Gemini API; for Database And Auth: Supabase PostgreSQL and pgvector; for storage: Supabase Storage.

Our project is creative because we reject the traditional structure, except for the scientific closeness to reign supreme in deciding the analogue. However, multiple factors are involved in deciding such analogue sites; creativity is built into the machinery of this platform in predicting the risk and suggesting ways to reduce it.

We have used different algorithms to make the decision, such as multi-criteria decision analysis, Pareto efficiency, minimax normalisation, etc. We aim to utilise global research in decision-making in the future in this platform and develop our own decision framework too, for which we need NASA's ecosystem.
dataRefs: NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRRO) / LOLA & NAC
